title: Seed-sweep shadow capture - perf sync (2026-01-14)
body:
Purpose:
Weekly perf/benchmarking sync focused on the mixed-sequence throughput regression observed in nightly bench on Jan 12. We ran a set of targeted shadow runs (seed-sweep) to isolate variability across trace seeds, batching heuristics, and kernel variants. This doc captures observations, hypotheses, and next actions.

Context / quick summary:
- Symptom: p95 latency increased ~30ms and sustained throughput dropped ~10-15% on mixed-length workload (user-proxy traces) compared to baseline from Dec. Baseline stable for months; regression appeared after kernel change + small scheduler tweak.
- When it happens: predominantly on mid-loads (QPS in 50-200 range) with mixed short/long sequences; cold-starts not required.
- Affected components: batcher queueing, prefix/KV cache hit rate, and attention kernel choice.

What we ran (test matrix):
1) Seeds: 8 different trace seeds (real-user-sampled and synthetic-mix). Each seed replayed across the same infra.
2) Batcher modes: legacy-naive, adaptive-window, and opportune-batcher (new heuristic).
3) Kernels: attention_v1 (baseline), attention_v2 (recent rollout), attention_v2_quant (int8).
4) HW targets: A100-40GB vs H100-80GB shadow hosts.
5) KV cache configs: ttl=5s, ttl=60s, enable-prefix-cache=true/false.

Key observations:
- Seed sensitivity: 2 of 8 seeds (seed-3, seed-7) consistently produced the worst p95 tails; these seeds have a high frequency of mid-length (200-400 tokens) prefix reuse patterns that trigger frequent KV cache evictions.
- Batcher interaction: opportune-batcher reduced mean latency slightly but increased tail (p99) by 12% for problematic seeds. Hypothesis: opportune-batcher batches together heterogeneous seq lengths causing longer serialization inside a few batches.
- Kernel variance: attention_v2 gave 6-8% throughput uplift on long-only workloads but regressed p95 on mixed workloads for two seeds when combined with int8 quantized path. The quantized path appeared sensitive to batch composition.
- HW note: H100 runs reduced absolute p95 by ~10ms but did not change the relative regression signal across seeds.
- KV cache: short TTL (5s) produced a spike in miss-rate during replay start, correlated with small priming bursts; long TTL (60s) improved steady-state hit-rate and reduced p95 by ~9% for the problematic seeds.

Evidence and artifacts:
- Sampled traces: attached in Confluence page (linked above).
- Flame snapshots: produced for attention_v1 vs attention_v2 for seed-3; attention_v2 shows a wider tail in kernel scheduling time slices.
- Logs: per-batch size histogram, queue-depth time series, and kv-cache hit/miss timelines uploaded to the perf S3 bucket under /seed-sweep/2026-01-14/.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Cache priming + small TTL causes periodic eviction storms that increase queue pressure and produce microbursts in latency for seeds with heavy prefix reuse. (High confidence)
2) New batcher heuristic increases heterogeneity inside batches for specific trace shapes, exposing quantized kernel path fragility. (Medium confidence)
3) attention_v2 scheduling changes interact poorly with our batcher pacing at mid QPS. (Medium-low confidence)

Triage experiments planned / in progress:
- A: Re-run seed-3 with kv-cache ttl=120s + opportune-batcher to test if long TTL eliminates the tail. Owner: Miguel Torres. ETA: 2026-01-22.
- B: Shadow-run attention_v2 with per-batch homogeneous enforcement (split long/short) to validate batch composition impact. Owner: Daniel Huang. ETA: 2026-01-21.
- C: Add fine-grained instrumentation to batcher: per-request enqueue timestamp + deque timestamp + kernel start; collect for next shadow run. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-01-20.
- D: Canary rollback of attention_v2_quant on a tiny % of traffic in staging and production shadow for 48 hours. Owner: SRE oncall. ETA: 2026-01-24.

Decisions from sync:
- Do not rollout attention_v2_quant further until we complete homogeneous-batch shadow and longer TTL experiment.
- Short-term config change: increase default prefix cache TTL from 5s -> 30s in shadow pool to reduce eviction noise while we run experiments. (Config PR: linked artifact)
- Add a perf gating checklist item before quantized kernel rollouts: must pass mixed-seq shadow runs on 3 diverse seeds.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Why are seed-3/7 trace shapes so common in production traffic patterns? Is there a higher-level traffic shift or a customer pattern (e.g., a new app usage)? (Action: product instrumentation request)
- Could we apply a fast-path early-exit for batches dominated by short sequences to avoid serialization delay? Cost/complexity unknown.
- Is the quantized kernel compilation introducing micro-scheduling variability (CUDA stream syncs) that isn't visible in coarse profiler? Need deeper GPU-level traces.

Action items (owners + short):
- Aisha: Add per-request enqueue/dequeue/kernel timestamps and sample p99 stack traces for problematic seeds. (ETA 2026-01-20)
- Miguel: Run long-TTL seed-3 replication and post results to perf S3. (ETA 2026-01-22)
- Daniel: Implement homogeneous-batch shadow harness (split by length) and compare attention_v1 vs v2. (ETA 2026-01-21)
- SRE: Prepare canary rollback plan and short-circuit for attention_v2_quant. (ETA 2026-01-24)
- Product: Investigate whether a new client behavior explains seed patterns (request: instrumentation ticket P-4301).

Meeting notes / decisions log:
- 2026-01-14 10:00 PT sync (Aisha/Daniel/Miguel/Lena) — agreed on short TTL bump in shadow and prioritized homogeneous-batch test.
- 2026-01-15 async: Miguel posted initial seed replay logs; noticed cache miss spike at 17:32.
- 2026-01-18: Aisha rolled instrumentation to staging; initial traces look promising (per-batch histograms show two-mode distribution).

Follow-ups (week):
- Collate results from Gi, run final comparison table (mean/p95/p99/throughput) across kernels and batcher modes. Goal: clear go/no-go for quantized rollout by 2026-01-28.
- If TTL bump reduces tail significantly, propose a config change path for Dedicated pools (document costs).

Notes to self / ephemeral thoughts:
- Revisit batching adaptive thresholds; maybe add a small heuristic: if first element in batch > X tokens, prefer homogeneous-build for Nms.
- Keep an eye on the interplay with cache warmers; warming strategy might be masked by TTL choice.

If you want raw run outputs, they're in the S3 bucket and I can paste a curated CSV (p95, p99, throughput) into this doc next update.

-- Aisha
